notes: Generally accurate; main weakness is occasional over-interpretive or awkward rendering of elliptical/technical phrases.
advice: Revise literal awkward spots: render “literis hu paucā committimus” as “we commit these few letters/characters to writing,” not “[examples].” For “necessarium ... iudicium secretius” use “the necessary secret tribunal/judgment,” not “more secret form.” “literis commendamus” should be “we transmit/record in writing,” not “entrust it to letters.”

notes: Generally accurate, but it inserts conjectural material and leaves one key phrase unresolved; some alphabet/table details are shaky.
advice: Remove unsupported additions such as “[conjectured: ordinary]” for “alphabeti nostri visualis”; translate it directly as “our visual alphabet” unless emending. Do not add “For example” unless taking “vig.” as “videlicet.” Resolve “confidetur ouiter alphabetum” cautiously as OCR-damaged, e.g. “another alphabet, reportedly/newly devised by a certain alchemist,” rather than “[unclear].” Recheck the numerical tables against the Latin columns, especially “et 6 q 80 9 1000 l9 30000” and “et 9 6000.”

notes: Strong overall; the specimen list is editorially compressed and misses distinctions such as epitola/litera/literae.
advice: Keep the main prose largely as is. In the list, preserve separate lemmata: render epitola as “epistle” (or mark OCR for epistola), litera as “letter,” and literae as “letters”; do not collapse them. quaeadmodu is better “in whatever manner/however” than only “[conjectured].” Consider translating notis as “shorthand signs/notes” consistently, since Cicero’s notae are technical tachygraphic signs.

notes: Very accurate overall, but adds editorial framing/footnote markers and overinterprets damaged names/sign labels.
advice: Remove unsupported editorial additions such as footnote markers and “The printed character rows follow.” For “Megalopyvirisapientissimi,” preserve the damaged compound/name more cautiously rather than normalizing to “Megalopyrus the Most Wise.” Render “sub or chemate/Orchena” as a damaged “schema/scheme” note only if marking conjecture consistently.

notes: Mostly accurate, but several [unclear]/conjectural insertions and one unjustified addition weaken fidelity.
advice: Remove unsupported additions: plurimorum is “of very many,” not “of very many of the ancients.” For “opus alterum alteri non praedicaret,” do not invent “[prejudice]”; render cautiously as “that one work should not proclaim/announce another, but its own due be allotted to each inviolate.” Resolve “sub nomine Iesu Christi” without “[unclear]”: “under the name of Jesus Christ.”

notes: Mostly faithful, but several OCR-damaged phrases are left unresolved and a few conjectures interrupt the translation.
advice: Resolve rather than bracket key phrases: for “leges, pari maiorum, mansuescere” render “to obey laws and the institutions of their ancestors, and to grow tame from former savagery.” For Adam’s “testamentum necessario moviendi,” give a cautious “a testament necessarily to be heeded/admonitory.” In Michael, replace “[unclear] began to regard their rulers as gods” with “they began to worship their rulers as gods” if reading “adorare principes.”

notes: Mostly accurate, but it adds conjectural material and mistranslates “vltimi/multi clarissimi viri” as “final men.”
advice: Remove unsupported footnote markers/headings if not wanted as translation. Render “maioribus terrae” as “the great men/nobles of the earth,” not “greater men.” Change “the most famous final men” for “vltimi/multi clarissimi viri” to “many very famous men.” “annos 364” should not silently become 354 unless marked as emending the print.

notes: Generally accurate, but adds unsupported conjectures and leaves “Et anq.” unresolved; “anno 1484 [before Christ]” is not in Latin.
advice: Remove unsupported bracketed additions, especially “anno 1484 [conjectured: before Christ]”; translate simply “in the year 1484.” Render “Et anq. variae regni Hebraorum mutationes” as “and there were also various changes in the kingdom of the Hebrews” rather than “[unclear].” Keep “Delphica” as “Delphic Sibyl” without marking conjecture if supplying the implied noun.

notes: Very accurate overall; only minor over-completion and one unresolved opening/cut-off phrase affect fidelity.
advice: Keep most wording. Resolve the opening “rurni magna in pace regnum continuit” from context rather than leaving “[unclear]” if the preceding page permits. For “Euil Merodach ... libertatem et regem populo restituit Hebraorum,” keep “restored liberty and the king to the Hebrew people.” At the end, “Denique ... bellis” is a page break, so avoid making it sound like a complete sentence; mark it as continuation rather than “Finally, in wars [unclear].”

notes: Mostly accurate, but leaves emendable OCR as bracketed uncertainty and misses 'in anno 463' near Anael chronology.
advice: Resolve obvious OCR instead of marking uncertainty: 'victimaeque' = 'victims/sacrificial offerings'; 'tertia vice' = 'for the third time'; 'Dominicae vero Nativitatis in anno 463' = 'in the 463rd year of the Lord's Nativity'; 'clarorum virorum' = 'distinguished men.' End with 'In Asia...' only because the source breaks off.

notes: Generally accurate, but a few damaged/crux passages are over-smoothed or left unresolved with [unclear].
advice: Keep the cautious handling of OCR damage, but revise cruxes more literally: for “Franci in Francorum Germanorum origo…” say “the Franks, the origin/beginnings of the Franks and Germans…”; for “quod ipse facere non potuit Raphaeli Angelo” do not add “left to” unless the continuation supports it. “maritimos fluctus pene tota submersa fuit” needs the missing subject from context, not just “[unclear].” Remove unsupported footnote markers if no notes are supplied.

notes: Generally accurate, but editorial footnote markers and some conjectural identifications add unsupported apparatus.
advice: Remove unsupported footnote markers and bracketed apparatus unless required. Translate “tari terras” as a damaged continuation, not confidently “Tatars,” unless supplied by context. Render “plus quam 4. centies Christianorum” without “[unclear]” as “more than four hundred Christians.” For “Ducatum de Spetis, Achaiam Mytsenam,” keep uncertain names closer to Latin: “the duchy of Spetis, Achaia, Mytsena,” rather than “Mycenae” if not certain.

notes: Generally accurate, but several corrupt/technical phrases are over-smoothed or left vague, especially Secareligionis and date wording.
advice: Revise corrupt but legible phrases more transparently: render “Secareligionis consurget magna” as something like “a great sect/schism of religion will arise,” not simply “[unclear].” For “mense 4. die mensis Iunij 4,” avoid “in the fourth month, on the fourth day of June”; say “in the fourth month, on June 4” or flag the date corruption. “satisfactionis consultae premium” is better “the price/recompense of negotiated satisfaction” than “reward duly considered.”

notes: Mostly accurate despite OCR damage, but leaves title terms unresolved and has a few over-literal/uncertain renderings.
advice: Resolve the heading rather than leaving broad “[unclear]”: render “abbatis Peazopolitani ... apud Sanctum Iacobum” as Trithemius’s abbacy/location if verified. Smooth “superfluous” to “unnecessary.” For “regumentis quibusdam operuimus figurarum,” use “covered with certain figurative coverings,” not conjectural “veils.” For “mentium suarum,” prefer “the thoughts/secrets of their minds,” not “purposes.”

notes: Generally tracks the damaged text, but several conjectures are overconfident and some OCR-cruxes are turned into unsupported specifics.
advice: Keep cruxes closer to the Latin. “dictioe p scole” should not be rendered confidently as “for the school”; mark uncertain or use “characters drawn for the words.” “Clodius… Romanũ sexntũcis” does not securely mean “Roman characters”; avoid that unless emended. “Brabũcia dũx… natus legitur” is better “is read to have been born in Brabantia, in the county of Namur…” not “born as duke of Brabant.”

notes: Broad structure is captured, but many [unclear] gaps and some added conjectural apparatus/footnotes go beyond the Latin.
advice: Remove unsupported footnote apparatus and bracketed scholarly conjectures unless translating supplied Latin. Render “literarum invisibilium” as “invisible letters,” not “visible letters.” Keep “Nanno grammatico ministrante” as “with Nanno the grammarian assisting.” For “fine voce loquebantur praesentibus,” use “spoke without voice to those present.” Reduce [unclear] by translating uncertain OCR cautiously rather than leaving whole phrases blank.

notes: Mostly tracks the passage, but several OCR-cruxes are over-translated and some unsupported framing/footnote material is added.
advice: Remove footnote markers not present in the Latin. Render “pellē induceres berculea, clauā…in manibus” as “put on Hercules’ skin, with club in hand.” Treat “latronibus suis spoliantur” as “are stripped by robbers,” not “their own robbers.” Rework “ne confusio…generetur”; “ecclesiastics” is likely an OCR error, not justified. Avoid translating garbled strings like “diercnes,” “infimue…” as meaningful prose unless marked as corrupt.

notes: Generally strong, but some [unclear] omissions and at least one likely reversal: “Nemo… scire poterit ubi reincepteris.”
advice: Revise the fourth caution: “Nemo… scire poterit ubi reincepteris” should be “no one, even moderately skilled in this procedure, will be able to know where you began again,” not “will be unable to know.” Avoid footnote-like conjectural framing in the translation; render “Cave tibi ab isto tiro… sed tace oro” directly as “Beware that novice… but keep silent, I beg.” “Thebontico” is better “Teutonic/German.”

notes: Generally accurate despite OCR damage, but some conjectural expansions and headings/footnote markers add material not in the Latin.
advice: Remove editorial headings/footnote markers unless allowed. For “Aufculdata sunt que ponuntur VIII” render more literally “The things set down in the eighth are to be listened to/heeded.” In XII, “reges…ac principes” is fine, but “uarii” likely “varios” = various servants/agents. Avoid unsupported “ruler” for “proprium.” In XIV, keep “quaedam praeceptis longe meliora” as “certain things far better than precepts,” not “contained.”

notes: Generally strong, but reverses the point in 'quibus otium placet ac displicet labor' and smooths some OCR cruces too freely.
advice: Revise 'apud illos maxime quibus otium placet ac displicet labor' as 'especially among those who like leisure and dislike labor,' not 'do not dislike labor.' Treat 'quatuor ... libris' cautiously as 'the four following books' if the print supports 'sequentibus.' For 'cuiusdam aedificii,' translate 'of a certain building' rather than leaving '[unclear]' if that is the intended reading.

notes: Generally accurate, but overuses conjectural brackets and slightly blunts phrases like intuentibus cautis and Caue hunc virum.
advice: Replace '[unclear]' only if you can account for the opening OCR debris; otherwise omit it from the assessed passage. Render intuentibus cautis as 'to careful observers,' not 'to ignorant observers.' For Caue hunc virum, give the full sense 'Beware this man'/'Beware of this man,' and avoid marking it conjectural since the following second-letter explanation supports it. Keep 'fabricated/coined words' for dictiones coctas.

notes: Mostly accurate, but it normalizes orchema as schema and invents/garbles the circular continuation passage.
advice: Revise “schema/schemata” to preserve the technical term: Latin has “orchema/orchematum,” glossed as Greek for Latin “transpositio.” Do not render “rurulis circuli facimus” as “we make the little wheels”; treat it as making/returning through the cycle. Replace “[unclear]” at “in auera 3” with the printed character or a diplomatic note, not an unexplained gap.

notes: Generally captures prose sense, but replaces both tables with summaries and adds unsupported footnote markers/conjectural framing.
advice: Do not omit the tabula numerorum or final alphabet: transcribe/translate their entries as far as legible rather than '[unclear table]'. Remove unsupported note markers (^1 etc.). Render 'orbe matu' consistently as 'moving wheel'; 'per transitiones et saltus' as 'by shifts and leaps'. For 'in imitatione quoque Nortmannorum' use 'also in imitation of the Normans'. Mark only truly illegible words as uncertain.

notes: Generally accurate, but several OCR-cruxes are left unresolved and a few phrases are over-specific or awkwardly conjectural.
advice: Revise OCR-cruxes into clean sense where recoverable: “latorem praesentium caveto” = “Beware the bearer of this letter/these presents,” not “present letter” awkwardly; “sententia” behind “fenetria” = “meaning/sense.” Avoid bracketed “[unclear]” where the Latin is readable, e.g. “calculation” for “supputationem.” For “in collo” likely read “in consilio”: “the king has decreed in council that you be killed.” Remove footnote markers unless notes are supplied.

notes: Main prose is mostly sound, but the first clause and much of the ternion table are left as meta-summary rather than translated.
advice: Remove the opening meta-preamble and translate what can be read: e.g. treat “quicquid naturalis sua voluerit industria uti prudenter” as “whoever wishes prudently to use his natural industry.” For “orchemate numerali,” keep a cautious “numerical arrangement/table,” not just “schema.” Render the colophon directly: “Explicit clavis Polygraphiae Ioannis Tritemii...” The table may be labeled as a cipher index, but translate its headings and entries line by line where legible rather than summarizing selected devotional words.

notes: Readable but too many unresolved OCR spots and some confident smoothing of damaged Latin into unsupported devotional sense.
advice: Revise the cipher instructions more literally: “sidnoddecima… sequens” should reflect taking the following/thirteenth letter, not “after the father.” In XXXI, do not render “amator cumtaes mundi vanities contentaes” as “content with all the vanities”; it means rejecting/despising worldly vanities. In XXXII, mark corrupt phrases like “piemant minuam,” “teverbosifimus rabulanque dominens,” and “tustiva” as corrupt rather than creating fluent theology from them.

notes: Large portions of Exemplum XXXIII are summarized or marked unclear instead of translated; Mode XXXIII secret is left in German.
advice: Translate, do not summarize, Exemplum XXXIII: render phrases like “precibus continuis et ... lectionibus scripturarum occupatus,” “temporalium ... procurator,” and “omnem levitatem animi muliebris deponentes.” Translate the Mode XXXIII German tenor too. Avoid adding “badly damaged in transmission” or footnote-style conjectures unless marked as editorial, and reconstruct Mode XXXIV alphabet from the stated rule: A=Q, B=R, C=S, D=T, E=U, etc.

notes: Handles the Marian controversy and cipher instructions partly, but over-conjectures damaged/nonsense passages and treats cipher filler as prose.
advice: Keep OCR-damaged/cipher padding visibly tentative. Do not smooth nonsensical words in Exemplum XXXV into coherent claims unless supported: e.g. “gandium calorum,” “beneslenitia,” “juuipli furere,” “canobijnotung” should remain marked corrupt or untranslated. Render “Tenor Secreti” simply as “The abbot of St. Johannesberg has dealings in common with the peasants, stays little in the monastery, and also rides/sails in the Ship of Fools.” For “prima ... in 16. permutatur,” say “the first [letter] of each significant word is changed by 16 places,” not merely “permuted to the sixteenth place.”

notes: Readable, but the corrupt example is over-literal and sometimes invents syntax, especially around a superbis and zelum amaritudinis.
advice: Revise the example more cautiously: do not render a superbis as “by the proud”; better “for the proud” or mark the construction corrupt. Keep pro xpo as “for Christ,” but temporalia likely belongs with contempt/emphasis on despising temporal things. For quoniam ... nihil aliud quam vanitatem querunt, avoid “from God” unless a Deo is certain. Treat humiles zelum amaritudinis elatione Christo as corrupt rather than supplying “humble men [unclear]...” Remove footnote markers not present in the Latin.

notes: Generally tracks the passage, but the damaged opening and cipher instructions are partly guessed and editorial comments are added.
advice: Revise the opening more cautiously: render “moribus d’gnis” as “by worthy morals” if taking it as dignis, not “[unclear] morals”; avoid “through humility” for “humilitate abiecit” unless explaining the syntax. In the cipher section, keep “prima significativae dictionis” as “the first [letter] of the significant word,” and avoid unsupported detail like “nineteenth following letter” if the Latin only says “in 19.” Remove or separate the editorial sentence about repeated “etc.”

notes: Mostly captures structure, but adds explanatory material and mishandles several cipher-rule details and the German secret.
advice: Keep the headings but remove editorial claims like “serving as the letter material.” Render “Etiam alternis utitur” as “It also uses alternating [words].” For “Porro si tertia prima cujuslibet dictio significativa…” preserve the damaged/odd text instead of inventing “[sequence].” “pro A capiatur x; pro b, c; pro e…” means “let x be taken for A; c for b; …” In the German, translate “du thust nicht” as “you are not to do [it]/do not do it,” not just “[unclear].”

notes: Generally tracks the OCR text, but smooths the corrupt Example LX and adds unsupported headings/footnote apparatus.
advice: Remove added apparatus like headings and footnote numbers unless requested. Keep corrupt phrases more literal: e.g. “Exemplum LX” is not a polished narrative; mark cruces around “quosque suis consensu,” “propter es hoffet,” and “annibales crueldati.” In Mode 40, render “vacua et significantia” as “null and significant words,” and “prima litera ... in 21” as a cipher shift, not “nearest following” unless justified by the alphabet.

notes: Generally tracks the method, but leaves many OCR cruces as [unclear] and adds headings/notes not in Latin.
advice: Remove editorial footnote markers and unsupported expansions. Render “viginti unus/21 modos,” not “twenty-one” only if Latin/OCR supports it; “singulis dictis/dictionibus significativis” = “individual significant words,” while heading says “singulis literis.” Translate “Potes[t] autem modus iste… multipliciter variari” directly. Do not translate the nonsense cover text semantically as polished prayer; present it as the Latin example text or mark it as cover text.

notes: Generally follows the cipher instructions, but adds apparatus/conjectures and mistranscribes key examples, especially fourth mode as 002 for Latin 001.
advice: Remove editorial footnote markers and unsupported '[conjectured]' intrusions from the translation. Correct 'Quartus sic 001...' to 'Fourth mode: 001 001...' not 002. Preserve cipher strings closer to Latin: e.g. 'Fmndpftens' where printed, 'Qmnrquasne' not 'Qmnruqasne'. Translate 'sigilla' as 'signs/seals' only if reading figlla as sigilla; otherwise flag OCR separately.

notes: Generally accurate; main weakness is making the cipher passages look unknowable rather than preserving them as transmitted text.
advice: Keep the cipher strings as transcribed rather than labeling them all “[unclear cipher sequence]”; they are part of the source. Render “perduo diuerfus” as “varied in two ways” or “diverse in two respects,” not “true form” unless supplying “form” silently. “cum aliis vocalibus interpolitus” is better “interpolated with other vowels.”

notes: Generally accurate, but it inserts conjectural/restorative material and some wording is overly literal or ambiguous.
advice: Remove or justify additions such as “[conjectured: opens his hand]” and footnote markers if not part of the task. Render “in cuius ditione cuncta sunt posita” clearly as God’s dominion, not the beasts’. Improve literal phrases: “gerit providentiam” = “exercises providential care,” not “bears providence”; “fortuito casu” = “by chance,” not “by fortuitous chance.”

notes: Mostly accurate, but bracketed conjecture around “periculorum...” adds uncertain content and two OCR cruxes are left unresolved.
advice: Resolve OCR cruxes instead of leaving bracketed meta. For “cuius confluum” likely read “consilium”: translate “whose counsel is never interrupted.” Do not write “[conjectured: he governs the causes of all dangers]” for “causam causarum...”/damaged “periculorum…”; keep only defensible sense: “as the exemplar of the universe and cause of causes, he provides for all things by knowing them.” Finish “Nec me fugit quam varie quondam huius mundi sapientes…” as “Nor am I unaware how variously the wise men of this world once…”

notes: Generally accurate, but the Boethius verse/prose is awkward and partly misread; final [unclear] is justified by the cutoff.
advice: Revise the Boethius passage: “Sede in terra” should not be “sits upon the earth”; render as “Meanwhile the high Creator sits and, ruling all things, bends the reins.” Smooth “repetuntque boni fine teneri” as “they seek to be held fast by the end/good.” Keep the closing cutoff marked as incomplete.

notes: Generally accurate, but leaves initial/final fragments unresolved and adds footnote apparatus not warranted by the Latin.
advice: Remove footnote markers and bracketed expansions. Resolve the opening around “contemnit ac negligit... nescientem nos” as continuous prose: “if he despises and neglects us, there is no reason...” Prefer “transgressors/offenders” for “desertoribus,” not “deserters.” At the end, “erigamus ab...” is incomplete because the sentence continues; translate only what is present: “let us raise our minds upward with whatever strength we can.”

notes: Strong overall, but adds/changes sense at “omnia potens potest” and mishandles “venia dignus”; place-name is uncertain.
advice: Revise “omnia potens potest” to “being omnipotent by nature, he can do all things,” not “all things that are possible.” Render “Faciat me venia dignus...” as “May it make me worthy of pardon if I have said anything less proper,” not “Let your pardon make me worthy.” Treat “Ex civitate Neometana” cautiously unless Neumarkt is independently justified.

notes: Very accurate and polished, but adds unsupported footnote markers and smooths a few OCR/crux readings too confidently.
advice: Remove note markers unless present in the source. Render opening damaged text more cautiously: “... will rule the rest, while truly knowing and wholly neglecting all else” rather than “[Unclear] rules...”. In Boethius, “rerumque regens flectit habenas” is “guiding/ruling the reins of things,” not “and, governing all things.” “fons et origo” not “oris go.” “desertoribus” should be “deserters/renegades” is fine; “rigit” is likely “igitur,” so “Therefore let men blush,” not “rigid men.”

notes: Very accurate and polished, but adds footnote markers/headings and misreads a few OCR-damaged phrases.
advice: Remove unsupported scholarly apparatus: footnote markers and '[conjectured: to it]' are not in the Latin. Render 'nobisipsis redacti vniamur' as 'having been brought back to ourselves, let us be united' without adding an object unless emending. 'quae cum sit...' refers to God's majesty/divinity, so 'which, since it is...' is safer than repeated 'it.' 'omnia potens potest' means 'being all-powerful, can do all things,' not 'all things that are possible.'

notes: Mostly accurate, but adds editorial material and reverses/over-conjectures “multorum facias iudicio improbari.”
advice: Remove footnote markers and the editorial “Damaged and Repeated Leaves” heading unless the edition requires apparatus. Render “viatori itinere constitutus” as “while set upon a journey” or “while traveling,” not “on a traveller’s road.” Treat “multorum facias iudicio improbari” cautiously: translate the transmitted Latin as “have them examined/tested by the judgment of many,” not simply “[approved].” “lucubratione mea” is better “this work composed by lamplight” than “little night-work.”

notes: Mostly accurate, but several OCR-damaged phrases are left unresolved and a few regimen details are weakened or mistranslated.
advice: Resolve more of the regimen: “so. noctib.” is likely a fixed number of nights, not just “[unclear] nights”; “vinum unius anni modice dilutum” should be “one-year-old wine, moderately diluted”; “prope somni horam” is likely “near bedtime.” Render “semen assumendum est” as “the prepared coriander seed should be taken,” and “memoriae caput/capsulam” more idiomatically as “the seat/region of memory,” not “capsule of memory.”

notes: Generally accurate, but the damaged opening and final syntactic crux are mishandled, with conjectures introduced into the text.
advice: Do not translate conjectures as main text unless signaled in the Latin: keep “Iro viri” and “mulieris dextro” cautiously unresolved rather than “[Moon]” and “right [eye].” In the last paragraph, revise “non omnino vna esse…”: likely “not altogether vain are the things…” rather than “not an entirely single efficacy.” Smooth “apud quodam” as an unfinished/damaged phrase, not “among certain persons [unclear].”

notes: Strong overall; main likely error is the syntax of “spiritus Dei naturae coadiuvatus,” not “assisting nature.”
advice: Revise “spiritus Dei naturae coadiuvatus per verbum Fiat”: coadiuvatus agrees with spiritus, so render “the Spirit of God, aided/assisted by nature through the word Fiat” (or flag the corrupt syntax), not “assisting nature.” “nominata constellata” can be simply “constellated names,” without the intrusive bracket if accepted as an emendation.

notes: Generally accurate, but adds conjectural/proper-name material and mishandles some corrupt technical phrases.
advice: Remove unsupported footnote markers and the added conjecture “from one source” for “et unu”; leave it unresolved or emend cautiously. Render “Philiatro” as “the lover/practitioner of medicine,” not a proper name. Revisit “cura characteristicae” as “characteristic healing/cure by characters,” and “nominata constellata” likely as names/characters made under a constellation, not “a named constellation.”
